sections.title: Fats
sections.narration: 13.9 grams of fat. Omega 3 is 2600 milligrams, supporting a more useful fat profile. Saturated fat is 3.3 grams, supporting a cleaner fat profile, but it is the smaller helper in this section. For meats, fat quality is the main tradeoff.

sections.title: Proteins
sections.narration: 18.6 grams of protein. Essential amino acids score is 9 out of 9, making the protein useful for repair and maintenance. Collagen is only 0.8 grams, not adding much structural protein, so for meats, that collagen side of the protein score stays weak. For meats, protein quality matters a lot.

sections.title: Vitamins
sections.narration: Vitamin B12 is 300% daily value, useful for nerve and blood-cell support. Vitamin D is 90% daily value, useful for bone and immune support, but it is not the standout here, so that's a small downside for meats. For meats, vitamin B12 and vitamin D matter most.

sections.title: Minerals
sections.narration: Iron is 9% daily value, the best number here but still too low to carry this section. Zinc is 6% daily value, not bringing much immune support. For meats, iron and zinc can add real value.
